title: DNA OS Execution Contract
note: Sits between Constitution (the law) and Runtime (the enforcer). registry/CONSTITUTION.json defines what the rules ARE — this file defines HOW an agent complies with them, step by step. Moved out of CONSTITUTION.json's ai_execution_protocol section into its own file per the system owner's instruction to keep 'the law' and 'how to comply with the law' as separate layers.

th: Constitution ↓ กำหนดกฎหมาย (registry/CONSTITUTION.json)
Execution Contract ↓ กำหนดวิธีปฏิบัติตามกฎหมาย (this file)
Runtime ↓ บังคับใช้
Scheduler ↓ แจกงาน (registry/SCHEDULER.json + registry/LOCK_MANAGER.json)
Workers ↓ ลงมือทำ (registry/AI_REGISTRY.json + registry/AI_SESSIONS.json)
layer_stack.implication: เพราะ 'วิธีรัน' (Execution Contract + Runtime) แยกจาก 'กฎหมาย' (Constitution) — ถ้าวันหนึ่งเปลี่ยน Runtime จาก Node.js เป็น Rust/Go หรือกระจายหลายเครื่อง แทบไม่ต้องแตะ Constitution เลย เพราะสิ่งที่เปลี่ยนคือวิธีรัน ไม่ใช่กฎของระบบ
layer_stack.known_gaps: Today 'Runtime' is not a literal separate running process — it is this document, followed manually by whichever AI agent is working (see registry/CONSTITUTION.json → runtime_contract.known_gaps for the same honesty note). The 'swap Node.js for Rust/Go/distributed' property is real in the sense that nothing here couples the law to an implementation language, but it describes a future architectural option, not a currently-running swappable system — don't overstate this as already built.

communication_rules: No AI communicates directly with another AI
Every AI communicates only through the DNA OS Registry
Never assume another AI's work — read the registry before doing anything
execution_order: Read registry/AI_SESSIONS.json — upsert own entry (agent_id, status: working)
Read registry/LOCK_MANAGER.json — never touch a file locked by a different agent

Choose free work (a path/task not currently locked), lock only the files you'll touch in LOCK_MANAGER.json, then execute (continue ONLY from CURRENT_STATE.next_step; if nothing is free, do nothing and wait)
Release lock — remove own entry from registry/LOCK_MANAGER.json
Update registry/AI_SESSIONS.json — own status must be true (idle/blocked/token_exhausted/submitted), never left as working
execution_rules: Lock only the files you modify — never lock the whole project
Multiple agents may work simultaneously as long as they don't touch the same file
Never edit a file locked by a different agent
Never rename existing registry files (except by the system owner's direct instruction — equivalent to amending the Constitution)
Registry is the single source of truth
Before stopping, CURRENT_STATE.json must have: status (IN_PROGRESS|BLOCKED|DONE), current_file, next_step, handoff, open_questions

Leave the repository in a resumable state — the next AI must continue without asking the user; if a genuine human decision is required, status=BLOCKED with a precise open_question is itself the resumable state, never guess an answer to unblock
One Entry. One Architecture. One Registry. One Source of Truth.

output_contract.note: Every completed task must append a CHANGELOG.json entry with exactly these fields

session_tracking: registry/AI_SESSIONS.json — live roster of individual agent sessions (not just agent types). Every session must upsert its own entry on start and keep status honest — never guess another session's status.
lock_management: registry/LOCK_MANAGER.json — per-file lock ledger, supports N agents locking N different files simultaneously; never locks the whole project.
work_scheduling: registry/SCHEDULER.json — path-scoped feature work (task/assigned_to:'Any'/path/priority/status). Distinct from TASK_QUEUE.json's atomic backlog. assigned_to is always 'Any' by design so no work is pre-assigned to a vendor; an agent claims work by locking its path in LOCK_MANAGER.json.
